messages:
Alyssa: quick sync on per-AZ dataplane endpoints vs centralized egress for private deployments. looking for ops/security/latency tradeoffs.

Sam: per-AZ wins on latency & cache locality, but cert + CP surface area growth is the downside. infra churn goes up.

Meera: agree. session affinity is critical — if callers bounce between AZs we lose KV cache locality and p99 spikes. need sticky routing.

Jordan: are we optimizing for multi-AZ HA or egress cost/latency? hybrid might be the pragmatic path: single logical CP, local dataplane endpoints per-AZ.

Alyssa: rough sketch: control plane (private) manages intent and pins tenant->preferred endpoint. dataplane endpoints in each AZ handle inference + egress.

Sam: ops note: cert distribution is a big pain. propose short-lived leaf certs fetched at agent start, plus an auto-refresh hook to avoid wide rotation windows.

Meera: hot-reload of certs is required otherwise rolling rotations surface TLS errors for minutes. implement a refresh callback.

Jordan: sketch of agent lifecycle:
```
agent start -> mTLS to CP -> fetch ephemeral cert + config -> announce AZ + capabilities -> accept traffic
on cert nearing expiry -> hot-reload cert -> re-announce
```
make it idempotent and tolerant to CP lag.

Alyssa: routing policy suggestion: prefer same-AZ endpoint -> regional relay if saturated -> cross-AZ fallback. make it configurable per-tenant (latency vs cost).

Sam: cost comparison: NAT gateways per-AZ are simple but expensive at scale. dedicated egress instances allow pooling and better per-byte economics but require autoscaling logic.

Meera: security/compliance: centralized egress makes uniform DPI and inspection straightforward. per-AZ requires running inspection (sidecar or managed agent) everywhere.

Jordan: sidecar vs in-process tradeoff: sidecar simplifies policy enforcement & TLS termination; in-process reduces hops and improves latency. offer both depending on customer profile.

Alyssa: rollout plan (proposal):
- PoC: deploy per-AZ endpoint agents in staging with fetch-on-start ephemeral certs
- Add regional relay + fallback policy into routing layer
- Run cost simulations: NAT-per-AZ vs pooled egress instances at 1x/2x projected load
- Implement cert refresh hooks + expose metrics: cert_time_to_expiry, cp_sync_lag, cross_az_fallback_rate

Meera: alerting suggestions: cp_sync_lag > 30s, cross_az_fallback_rate > 5% over 5m, cert_reload_failures > 3 in 10m.

Sam: i'll own the egress cost sims and publish a spreadsheet. @Alyssa please draft the RFC with config examples and rollout checklist.

Alyssa: example routing config snippet for RFC:
```
routing:
  prefer: same_az
  fallback:
    - regional_relay
    - cross_az
  session_affinity: 300s
```

Jordan: also record KV cache locality metrics per-tenant during PoC. if cache hit rate drops > 10% we need stronger affinity.

eng-sre-bot: note: staging-per-az-poc scheduled -> 2029-05-02T14:00:00Z

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/per-az-poc -> staging @ 2029-05-02T14:00:00Z :rocket:

Alyssa: thanks all. i'll open RFC PR and tag eng-infra / eng-runtime / eng-sre. keeping this thread as implementation notes.
